MIGRATION 015 (design sections 7.1-7.4), additive to 006. (a) 7.1: PUBLISHED joins the allowed base states BUILDING | VALIDATING | READY | PUBLISHED for product registration, BUILDING product rows and chunk receipts, and for BUILDING -> READY/FAILED; every other 006 rule stays (product starts BUILDING; identity and manifest immutable; READY needs a VERIFIED receipt; FAILED needs evidence; product data and receipts insert-only; RETIRED/FAILED bases reject attachment and writes; products have no VALIDATING state). (b) 7.2: ALTER TABLE v3_meta.derived_product ADD COLUMN published_at timestamptz (NULL = unpublished, one-way NULL -> one timestamp, never changed or cleared); CREATE TABLE v3_meta.derived_product_publication_audit exactly as written in 7.2 with UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE rejected. The invariants live in the table guards: the BEFORE UPDATE lifecycle guard on derived_product gains a publication branch for NEW.published_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.published_at (no other column may change; old value NULL; takes advisory transaction lock 764003001; the row's generation is the current pointer AND PUBLISHED; the product is READY with a VERIFIED receipt; the new value equals transaction_timestamp()); a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger requires at commit an audit row with the exact generation, product, version, manifest hash and timestamp and re-verifies the base is still the current PUBLISHED generation; the product INSERT guard requires published_at IS NULL; the audit INSERT guard requires at commit that the product row's published_at equals the audit timestamp and its version and manifest hash match. v3_meta.publish_derived_product(generation_id uuid, product_code text, actor text) -> timestamptz is the audited convenience path exactly as 7.2 lists its steps. (c) 7.3: recreate v3_app.system_search, v3_app.system_archetype and v3_app.system_archetype_summary to join the current PUBLISHED generation to its product row and require lifecycle_state = 'READY' AND published_at IS NOT NULL (the wide-row views from the rewritten 011 are the base; keep every column they expose). (d) 7.4: publish_derived_generation takes the incoming products to publish as an argument and in one transaction verifies each is READY/VERIFIED, moves the pointer and retires the outgoing generation, publishes each named product through the same routine publish_derived_product uses, then evaluates the counterpart rule and the unfinished-product rule (each raising its own distinct error) so a violation rolls the flip back; 015 executes DROP FUNCTION on the old seven-argument signature v3_meta.publish_derived_generation(uuid, uuid, bigint, uuid, bigint, text, text) in the same transaction so it cannot be called without the rules; the pointer table v3_meta.current_derived_generation gets a BEFORE UPDATE row trigger taking pg_advisory_xact_lock(764003001), a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger evaluating at commit exactly what the function checks (new target READY with VERIFIED receipt or an eligible RETIRED generation on the current canonical generation, different from the old target, publication_sequence = old + 1, old target RETIRED and new target PUBLISHED in the same transaction, a matching derived_publication_audit row, both Finder rules), statement triggers rejecting TRUNCATE and DELETE, and a BEFORE INSERT row trigger allowing INSERT only into an empty table under the same lock and deferred contract with no old target and publication_sequence = 1. Because a row-level BEFORE INSERT trigger fires for every proposed row of INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, the publisher must use a plain UPDATE once the singleton exists. The pre-010 READY system_search on ratings_v4_prod_p4_opt1 keeps a NULL published_at and stays invisible because opt1 is not current. The migration is one transaction; the migration runner commits it with its ledger row.

The archetype builder's requirement that the same generation's system_search be READY/VERIFIED stays. Neither builder publishes anything.
